overarching_problem.summary: A deep-space listening post picks up a repeating, garbled transmission. The crew (Mathematician + Friend + You) has to intercept and decode it to find the source.

chapter_missions.mission: Decode the raw signal (it arrives as pairs of numbers)
Correct the ship's course to follow the signal's bearing, which requires repeated rotations
Plan safe burn windows so the ship doesn't overshoot or collide while chasing it
Crack the signal's final cipher, which turns out to be a polynomial encoding the destination coordinates

chapters.name: Complex Numbers
chapters.subtitle: Decoding the Signal

topics.topic: Complex number as an ordered pair
topics.story_beat: The signal arrives as raw pairs of numbers with no context
topics.why_in_story: Establishes: a complex number isn't mystical, it's just an ordered pair — exactly what the raw data looks like

topics.story_beat: Two signal fragments need to be combined to make sense
topics.why_in_story: Motivates add/subtract/multiply/divide as the tools to merge fragments

topics.story_beat: The ship's onboard computer needs a standard notation to log the decoded pairs
topics.why_in_story: Converts the raw pair into a usable working format

topics.story_beat: Crew needs to know how strong the signal is and in what direction it's coming from
topics.why_in_story: Modulus = signal strength, Amplitude/argument = bearing angle — directly usable, not abstract

topics.story_beat: Plotting the decoded signal gives the crew a literal star-map bearing to steer toward
topics.why_in_story: Pays off the whole chapter — the abstract numbers become a heading on a screen

chapters.chapter_close: Crew now has a heading. Problem: getting there requires the ship to rotate repeatedly to align with that heading — which the Mathematician says needs a different tool.

chapters.name: De Moivre's Theorem
chapters.subtitle: Course Correction

topics.topic: De Moivre's Theorem — integral & rational indices
topics.story_beat: Ship needs to compute the result of many repeated rotation burns without simulating each one individually
topics.why_in_story: Direct payoff: raising a complex number to a power = the shortcut for repeated rotation

topics.topic: nth roots of unity, geometric interpretation
topics.story_beat: Crew discovers the signal source isn't one point — it's broadcasting from several evenly-spaced relay stations in a circle
topics.why_in_story: Roots of unity are literally equally spaced points on a circle — visual and narrative click perfectly here

chapters.chapter_close: Ship is now on course toward the relay stations. But fuel is limited — the crew needs to plan exactly when and how hard to burn thrust, or they'll overshoot or run dry.

chapters.name: Quadratic Expressions
chapters.subtitle: The Burn Window

topics.topic: Quadratic expressions & equations in one variable
topics.story_beat: Fuel-burn trajectory naturally comes out as a quadratic — Friend models distance vs time for the burn
topics.why_in_story: Grounds the quadratic in a real curve the crew can see on a screen, not an abstract equation

topics.topic: Sign of quadratic expressions, max/min values
topics.story_beat: Crew needs to know: does the trajectory ever go negative (i.e. crash course)? What's the most fuel-efficient point?
topics.why_in_story: Sign changes = danger zones, max/min = the optimal burn moment — stakes make the concept concrete

topics.story_beat: Mission control defines a safe corridor — the trajectory must stay within a range, not hit one exact value
topics.why_in_story: Naturally frames inequations as a range the ship must stay inside, not just an equation to solve

chapters.chapter_close: Ship arrives safely. Now the crew has the full signal and must crack its final cipher — which the Mathematician reveals is a polynomial equation.

topics.story_beat: The cipher is a polynomial — Friend shows you can extract clues about the destination without fully solving it, just from the coefficients
topics.why_in_story: Real payoff: roots-and-coefficients tricks feel like an actual codebreaking shortcut

topics.topic: Solving equations when roots are connected by a relation
topics.story_beat: The alien cipher includes a hint: two of the coordinates are related (e.g. one is double the other)
topics.why_in_story: Directly mirrors how these problems are normally posed — now it's a decryption clue instead of a textbook instruction

topics.topic: Real coefficients — complex roots in conjugate pairs
topics.story_beat: Some decoded coordinates come out complex — Friend explains why they always arrive in pairs
topics.why_in_story: Ties directly back to Chapter 1's complex numbers — nice narrative full-circle

topics.story_beat: Final step: the cipher needs to be transformed into a related equation to reveal the true coordinates
topics.why_in_story: Climax — this is the module that solves the mission

story_resolution: Crew decodes the final coordinates, arrives at the source, mission complete. Each sub-topic was a tool the crew needed, in the order they needed it.
